data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra, having raised $11.5M to date. The broader sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient depth at Karman's specific stage and valuation tier to support a robust median-based valuation.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total raised ($11.5M, rounded to $12M as a proxy for post-money valuation at Seed entry) and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage, this method yields $29M. A sensitivity band around this point estimate—accounting for typical variance in Seed-stage progression rates—produces a low bound of $24M and a high bound of $33M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M to $33M, with a median of $29M. This triangulation rests on a single applicable methodology. Key uncertainties include (1) the actual post-money valuation at initial Seed close, which may differ from raised capital; (2) the applicability of standard 2.5x progression assumptions to frontier-tech capital efficiency; and (3) the absence of tight peer comparables for cross-validation. Refinement would benefit from additional founder context, burn rate, and a larger or more precisely filtered peer dataset.
